nobody really tells you this about AI creative work...

The image might take 30 seconds to generate.

Getting to that image? 😅
That can take weeks.

I recently spent almost 3 weeks building a merchandising system for a campaign.
12 master templates.
2 backgrounds.
3 poses.

1 character that had to stay consistent across everything.
The final images were honestly the easiest part.
What took forever was figuring out why things kept breaking.

Lighting.
Composition.
Prompt structure.
Character consistency.
Product accuracy.

40+ failed generations? Easily. Probably way more 😂

That's the part nobody posts.
People see the final image and think, "AI did it."

I wish it was that simple.

For me, the real work happens before I even hit Generate.

It's the planning, testing, art direction, rebuilding, throwing ideas away, and starting again.

And lately... I've been thinking a lot about how I share my work.

AI regulations are changing.

Clients are asking different questions.

And let's be honest... a lot of people really don't like AI. 😅

Some people will scroll past the second they see "Made with AI."

Others are genuinely curious about how it's actually used in a professional workflow.

So I think I'm going to start showing more of that.

Less "look what AI made."

More "here's what it actually took."

Not because I'm trying to convince anyone to like AI.

But because I think the process is honestly more interesting than the final image.

Maybe it'll help people understand why brands aren't paying for a prompt...

They're paying for the thinking behind it.

Anyway... still figuring this out as I go. 🙂

Does anyone else working with AI feel this too? Or is it just me? 👀

Imagine if Pandora... 

...didn't launch a collection. It launched an entire world.🌊✨

I've been genuinely obsessed with the new Pandora Wonders collection. 
The organic baroque pearls, playful sea-inspired charms, and incredible craftsmanship instantly made me think beyond the product itself. Instead of asking "How would I photograph this?" I found myself asking, "Where would this charm live?"

That single question completely changed the creative direction.
Rather than creating standalone product visuals, I imagined a surreal universe where every Pandora Wonder belonged to its own magical ecosystem. Floating oyster sanctuaries. Sapphire mirror oceans. Impossible underwater landscapes. Every image became another chapter in the same story instead of another AI-generated render.

❓ One thing AI has taught me is that the strongest campaigns don't start with prompts they start with world-building. Once you define the world, the visual language follows naturally. The color palette becomes consistent. The lighting feels intentional. The camera choices make sense. Every asset shares the same creative DNA, making the campaign feel cohesive rather than generated.

That's the mindset I try to bring into every project. AI isn't just a faster way to create images it's a tool for building entire creative systems that can scale while maintaining a strong, recognizable identity.

I'm excited to share more of the process behind this campaign over the coming days, from world-building and campaign DNA to the prompt architecture that keeps every image visually consistent

👇 If you'd like me to break down exactly how I built thisfrom campaign DNA and world-building to prompt architecture and cinematic workflows comment "WONDER" and I'll share the entire process.

What brand or product do you think deserves its own surreal universe? 👇
